notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix for the phrase order (PB5102 owns the neighbouring §1985:IX.4.5.3 SR5 defect, a dynamic-access READ ... AT END accepted without NEXT, which is that rule's row and not this format's). §1985:IX.4.5.2 prints two formats: Format 1 READ file-name-1 [NEXT] RECORD [INTO identifier-1] [AT END ...] [NOT AT END ...] [END-READ], and Format 2 READ file-name-1 RECORD [INTO identifier-1] [KEY IS data-name-1] [INVALID KEY ...] [NOT INVALID KEY ...] [END-READ]. The one superset rule readStatement keeps the printed order of NEXT, RECORD, INTO and KEY IS (INTO after KEY IS, or RECORD after INTO, is COBOL2269), and the two formats are kept apart by ConditionalPhraseAssociation (the Owners row of readStatement: the AT END pair is not printed beside KEY IS, the INVALID KEY pair not beside NEXT, and never both pairs) and by BindRead with CheckReadRandomAccessPhrases and CheckReadKeyFormat (NEXT or AT END on a random-access file, INVALID KEY or KEY IS on a sequential-access file: COBOL1720, COBOL0864). The later editions' additions are refused at 85 on recognition, each COBOL0900: PREVIOUS (VisitReadDirection), IGNORING LOCK, WITH [NO] LOCK and ADVANCING ON LOCK (VisitReadIgnoringLock, VisitRecordLockPhrase, VisitReadAdvancingOnLock), RETRY (VisitRetryPhrase). All of that was probed at --std 85. What is NOT implemented is the printed sequence inside each phrase pair: the conditionalPhrases loop and Associates / MayAssociate ask only that a phrase is printed by a format and not yet written, with no edition arm, so NOT AT END before AT END and NOT INVALID KEY before INVALID KEY compile at 85; either order is the 2002 change §2002:F.2 item 33 ("The conditional phrases in the ... READ ... statements may be specified in any order"), which the row's change record also names. Same mechanism as the DELETE, REWRITE, START and WRITE rows of this slice. The witness runs both formats in the printed order (Format 1 with and without NEXT, Format 2 with and without KEY IS and RECORD).

next.reason: 1985 indexed READ: Format 1 READ file-name-1 [NEXT] RECORD [INTO] [AT END] [NOT AT END] [END-READ]; Format 2 READ … [KEY IS data-name-1] [INVALID KEY] [NOT INVALID KEY] [END-READ]. §2023:14.9.30.2 adds PREVIOUS, ADVANCING ON LOCK, IGNORING LOCK, WITH [NO] LOCK, retry-phrase and record-key-name-1, and its choice indicators let AT END/NOT AT END and INVALID KEY/NOT INVALID KEY appear in either order; §2023:14.9.30.3 SR8 and SR9 state when the omitted NEXT is implied ("the NEXT phrase is implied"). Every 1985 READ keeps its meaning; cases are added at compile time.
